prose.title: L.A. Looks Tagged Amon-Ra St. Brown, Traded Him, and Bought George Pickens
prose.dek: Ryan Bousquet used his biggest tag as a trade chip, took Sam Darnold for it, then paid {{f.team.0001.faa_15762_price}} for the Pickens that C-Town had let go. The preseason simulation ranks L.A. Looks {{f.team.0001.power_rank|ord}}.

paragraphs: April was thin and cheap. Bousquet carried {{f.team.0001.active_roster_opening}} active players and only {{f.team.0001.cap_opening}} in salary, and one top-twelve starter, Chase Brown at running back. Bo Nix and Jake Ferguson were solid. The {{f.team.0001.holes_opening}} holes were Zach Charbonnet at the second running back spot, Alec Pierce and Courtland Sutton at receiver, Tank Bigsby and Jauan Jennings in the flexes, and Carson Wentz in the superflex.

The early moves were about money. In April David Montgomery and his {{f.team.0001.trade1_salary_out}} salary went to HammerTime for a 2027 second, and in May Brown's rookie deal was extended at {{f.team.0001.contract_16181_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0001.contract_16181_tcv}} in all. Brown was one of {{f.team.0001.expired_rookies}} rookie deals running out. {{f.team.0001.expired_to_era}} of the others went to the Expired Rookie Auction, where Bousquet bought Charbonnet and Bigsby back and let Brian Branch and Michael Mayer go to C-Town and Real Deal Creel.

t.0001.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: The tags were the story. Bousquet tagged Kamren Curl at {{f.team.0001.tag_15001_salary}} and Amon-Ra St. Brown at {{f.team.0001.tag_15287_salary}} in May, and St. Brown turned out to be exactly what a tag is in this league, a chip. In July he went to Gride with Shedeur Sanders and {{f.team.0001.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money for Sam Darnold, Jalen Coker and Emmett Johnson, and the deal moved {{f.team.0001.trade4_salary_out}} of salary out and {{f.team.0001.trade4_salary_in}} in. A top receiver on a one-year tag became a starting quarterback and room for the auction.

Around it, the draft and the Expired Rookie Auction filled out the roster. On draft day he traded 3.08 to HammerTime for 4.08, 5.01 and a 2027 fourth, then made {{f.team.0001.rookie_picks_count}} picks, starting with Bryce Lance at 3.10. At the Expired Rookie Auction he paid {{f.team.0001.era_16169_price}} to keep Charbonnet and {{f.team.0001.era_16164_price}} for Bigsby, and bought Jordan Battle and Marvin Mims, then sent Battle and Adonai Mitchell to the Long Haulers in July for Isaiah Bond and a 2027 fourth. No cuts. The roster went into the auction at {{f.team.0001.active_roster_preauction}} active players and {{f.team.0001.cap_preauction}} in salary.

t.0001.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: Then he bought back the receiver he had traded away, in a different body. George Pickens, released by C-Town on lock day, cost {{f.team.0001.faa_15762_price}} after eleven bids, the biggest of {{f.team.0001.faa_lots_won}} wins that came to {{f.team.0001.faa_spend}}. Daniel Jones cost {{f.team.0001.faa_14059_price}} and Jaylen Warren {{f.team.0001.faa_15742_price}}.

Pickens is the one buy that changed the lineup, a Mid WR1 and the only Very good entry in the What it bought column. Jones is a backup quarterback and Warren a Low-end RB3, and for all that money the league table ranks the auction {{f.team.0001.faa_off_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}} for what each dollar added.

The contracts came late. Pickens got a multi-year deal in September, days before the opener, {{f.team.0001.contract_15762_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0001.contract_15762_tcv}} in all, and so did Charbonnet at {{f.team.0001.contract_16169_tcv}} and Mims, the two Expired Rookie Auction buys. Alec Pierce was extended at {{f.team.0001.contract_15768_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0001.contract_15768_tcv}} in all, and Darnold's deal was restructured after the auction to {{f.team.0001.contract_13592_salary}} this year. He claimed Chris Brooks off waivers and released Wentz, Riley Leonard and Troy Franklin at no cost, and he is down to {{f.team.0001.cap_current_room}} of room.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0001.studs_today}} top-twelve starters, Brown and Pickens, with Nix, Ferguson and Darnold solid, and {{f.team.0001.holes_today}} holes: Warren at the second running back spot, Pierce at receiver, Sutton in a flex and Isaiah Likely, a replacement-level tight end, in the other. The defense is a footnote, but a good one: over the last three seasons his defenders have scored more per start than anyone's.

captions.t.0001.faa_value: Ranked by how much each owner's starting offense improved between the auction lock and the close, for every dollar he spent on quarterbacks, backs, receivers and tight ends at the Free Agent Auction. What it bought sorts those buys by grade at their position: Elite, Very good, Good or Depth.

paragraphs: Bousquet is an original, here since {{f.team.0001.hist_first_season}}, and the record is a winner's: titles in {{f.team.0001.hist_title_years}}, runner-up finishes in {{f.team.0001.hist_runner_up_years}}, {{f.team.0001.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips in {{f.team.0001.hist_seasons}} seasons, and {{f.team.0001.hist_div_titles}} division titles. His career all-play record is {{f.team.0001.hist_allplay_pct}}.

Maddie Mondays is a division of champions on paper and middleweights in the simulation. Sex Manther, champion in {{f.league.title_years_0007}}, is {{f.league.power_rank_0007|ord}}; Real Deal Creel is {{f.league.power_rank_0008|ord}}; and L.A. Looks is {{f.team.0001.power_rank|ord}}, with {{f.team.0001.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and a {{f.team.0001.sim_p_division}} chance at the division. Bousquet plays Creel and Manther five times each.

The next three years, as a progress report to his Esteemed Colleagues. 2027: L.A. Looks shows a growth mindset. Pickens is a top receiver, Darnold is the answer, and Manther and Creel are informed, at length, in the group chat. 2028: a third title, and a victory lap made entirely of movie quotes. 2029: the retirement speech, delivered as a GIF.
Week one has been quiet so far: {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done and {{f.team.0001.wk_points_final}} points in the bank, with Darnold held to almost nothing through the air in the opener.
